title: Major Chinese Archaeological Exhibitions Could Come to Mexico as a Heritage Exchange
author: Arturo Sánchez and Alonso Urrutia
content:
_This article by Arturo Sánchez and Alonso Urrutia originally appeared in
the[August 21, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/08/21/cultura/mexico-y-china-
buscan-el-intercambio-de-exposiciones-arqueologicas-como-parte-de-estrategia-
diplomatica), Mexico’s premier left-wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City**. Mexico and China are holding talks for **major Chinese
archaeological exhibitions to come to Mexican territory** , as part of a
heritage exchange that has so far taken Mexican pieces to three exhibitions in
Chinese cities, the director general of the National Institute of Anthropology
and History (INAH), Joel Omar Vázquez Herrera, reported this Friday at the
morning press conference at the National Palace.

Vázquez Herrera detailed that the three Mexican archaeological exhibitions
held in China since 2024 have together drawn **nearly 2.9 million visitors**.
The first, called _Ancient Mesoamerica, Nature and Art_ , was presented in
Beijing during 2026 and registered an attendance of 200,000 visitors, the
official noted.

The second, titled _Ceiba and Cosmos_ , dedicated to the Maya people, was
exhibited in three Chinese cities between 2025 and 2026, with 1.5 million
visitors, the largest attendance among the three shows.

The third, _The Jaguar, Totem of Mesoamerica_ , also hosted in those three
Chinese cities, corresponded to 2024 and drew 1.2 million visitors.

![Visitors view Mesoamerican pieces at the exhibition in
China](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-21-mexico-china-
exhibitions-02-visitors.jpg)Chinese visitors take in Mexican archaeological
pieces at the exhibition in China. Photo: CNMyE-INAH

The INAH director added that the exhibition _Sacred Spaces_ is currently on
display at the Shanghai Museum, inaugurated on July 8, which has registered
300,000 visitors so far in August 2026 and will remain open until November
2027.

The show brings together **804 pieces** from the Olmec, Teotihuacan, Maya and
Mexica cultures: 745 come from INAH’s collections, 46 from the Archaeological
Museum of Xalapa, in Veracruz, and 13 from the Amparo Museum, in Puebla.

![Mesoamerican sculptures on display at the exhibition in
China](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-21-mexico-china-
exhibitions-03-sculptures.jpg)Mesoamerican sculptures on display during the
Mexican exhibitions in China. Photo: CNMyE-INAH

Among the pieces sent to Shanghai, Vázquez Herrera mentioned the Mexica
sculpture of Mictlantecuhtli, found in 1994 in the House of the Eagles at the
Templo Mayor, made of clay with the fleshless face of the deity; the Lord of
Las Limas, an Olmec carving in green stone located in the 1960s in the
municipality of Jesús Carranza, Veracruz; the funerary trousseau of Pakal the
Great, found in 1952 in the Temple of the Inscriptions at Palenque, Chiapas,
made of jade and comprising a death mask, ceremonial belt, necklace and
pectoral; and a Teotihuacan sculpture of a founding ancestor, in green stone,
dated between the years 200 and 250 AD, located in 2014 in the tunnel beneath
the Temple of the Feathered Serpent, in Teotihuacan.

![A gallery of the Mexican archaeology exhibition in
China](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-21-mexico-china-exhibitions-04-gallery.jpg)A
gallery of the Mexican archaeology exhibition in China, with signage reading
“From the Olmecs to the Aztecs.” Photo: CNMyE-INAH

The official described the exchange with China as “a strategy of diplomatic,
cultural relations that allows us to share, above all in this case with
another millenary culture like China’s, heritage exchanges that will allow us,
above all, to show the great richness of Mexico abroad, in this case in
China.” He specified that, in parallel, “we are in talks for grand exhibitions
from China to come to national territory.”

Vázquez Herrera indicated that, adding the three exhibitions in China to two
others already concluded in Spain and France, plus the current show in
Shanghai, the total number of visitors to Mexican archaeological exhibitions
abroad rises to **3.8 million**.

![Scenes from the Mexican archaeological exhibitions in
China](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/08/2026-08-21-mexico-china-
exhibitions-05-collage.jpg)Scenes from the Mexican archaeological exhibitions
in China, from Olmec and Zapotec sculptures to a Teotihuacan mural gallery.
Photos: CNMyE-INAH
